findings.text: the repair fixed the id-set construction in dispatch.py's _plan_section_text but left the identical construction in _contains_plan_section (routing.py:1247: ids = {requested_folded.removeprefix("#"), section_record_id(requested)}), and reckon/crew/routing.py is inside this node's own declared write paths (orientation_write_paths lists it). I probed the function at ebd212e9a with a plan whose heading id is the dotted anchor and whose heading text omits the reference: _contains_plan_section returns False for the reference spelling ('§5.1') against a dotted anchor (id="s5.1") while it returns True against the hyphen anchor (id="s5-1"), so a plan authored under a literal dotted anchor has no direct-id resolution for its own reference there. No live failure results: every dotted-anchor plan on this workstation (docs/plans/crew-effort-routing.html id="s5.1", self-hosted-worker-backends.html id="s1.1") prints the reference in the heading, so the heading-text fallback still resolves them; the direct-id path is the narrower one, exactly the defect repaired in the sibling function this round.

the routing.py follow-on's stated reason ('left untouched because routing.py is outside this round's write scope') is contradicted by this node's own record: orientation_write_paths lists reckon/crew/routing.py among its nine declared paths and the node's changed_paths include it. Whether it is a repair-round sub-scope or the node's, a reader checking the declared boundary from the record is told the sibling narrowing sits outside scope when the declaration says otherwise; the accurate statement is that the same narrowing remains in a file the node owns.

the record states plainly (landing line 13, evidence_inputs line 24) that live host flight.yaml (~/.config/reckon/flight.yaml) declares no by_capability_class overlay, so the shipped capability_raise resolves no lane change on this workstation until a host layer declares one; this is a config decision the node records, not a code defect, but a reader should not take the passing gate as evidence that live dispatches are being raised.

justifications.durability: The guarded thing is made to happen and the refusal is shown. I copied the repair head ebd212e9a into a scratch tree, reverted exactly the repair's dispatch.py id-set block to its pre-repair content, and the added case test_a_dotted_anchor_is_reachable_from_every_spelling reddens with EXIT=1, 1 failed/4 passed (logs/reviewer-negative-control.log; scratch, PYTHONPATH pinned, python -P so the terminator of judgements pins the reference spelling). With the repair in place the same probe resolves both the dotted anchor and the reference (logs/reviewer-head-gate.log, 148 passed/2 skipped). The base arm fails the four added dispatch-routing cases rather than erroring at collection, and the assertions compare against literals rather than a value the test handed the code.
justifications.evidence: Both arms completed to their summary lines with revision/command/exit_status/completed/failure_count/failure_ids: base-gate.log at 33c5e761d reports 4 failed/143 passed/2 skipped (the change's own four added cases) and head-gate-repaired.log at the reviewed head ebd212e9a reports 148 passed/2 skipped EXIT=0, so parsing the two logs gives added_failure_ids = after_failures minus base_failures = [] and added_failure_count 0. I re-ran the four-file gate myself at ebd212e9a and reproduced 148 passed/2 skipped EXIT=0 (logs/reviewer-head-gate.log), and the after-arm now names the reviewed head; the earlier round's after-arm revision mismatch (4fba21b2a) is repaired. The wider crew-dispatch regression set is now measured at both matched revisions (head 15 failed/240 passed at ebd212e9a, base 17 failed/238 passed at 33c5e761d); parsing both logs, every head failing id also fails at base, so head-only ids are none, and the two base-only ids are watcher-arming cases whose outcome flips with the live fleet's watcher state.
justifications.fit: The change follows the repository's idioms: the tests synthesise a temporary repository and point RECKON_HOME at a temp config home rather than reading or writing the real one, the four duplicate record-identity derivations collapse onto routing.section_record_id/section_anchor, the repair's comment names the anchor grammar rather than a plan label, ruff adds no finding over the base and removes 107 (UP045 zeroed by the regeneration). Docked two: the repair brought the both-spellings id lookup to dispatch.py but not to the identical _contains_plan_section in routing.py, a file this node declared and edited, and the follow-on that records the gap states a scope boundary the record's own write paths contradict.
justifications.goal_fidelity: Plan section 5's done-when is met on the production dispatch path, not merely a routing helper: plan_dispatch resolves section_routing from the repair-and-shipped config and takes the backend the raised class maps to, so a section at attempts 3 dispatches on the raised class's lane with the summary naming the count and a section at attempts 2 resolves unchanged. The repair round additionally makes the section-text lookup admit both authored anchor spellings. I reproduced the four-file gate green at ebd212e9a (148 passed, 2 skipped, EXIT=0) and confirmed the attempts-3/attempts-2 split and the dotted/hyphen spelling parity directly against the imported module.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --name-only 33c5e761d ebd212e9a lists seven files, every one inside the manifest's nine declared write paths; the repair round confines itself to reckon/crew/dispatch.py and the test file (2 files, 32 insertions, 1 deletion), the reviewed worktree HEAD is ebd212e9a with a clean status, the worker committed locally with a conventional subject and a body and did not push, merge or mutate the plan/index/sprint state, and the heavy gate ran under the pinned interpreter with a /tmp basetemp.
